In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a high-speed, high-resolution CCD-based particle detector for a future linear collider.
the development of high-speed serial readout CCDs for the tracking detectors of the International Linear e(+)e(-) collider (ILC).
the design and development of CCDs for high energy physics experiments at a future linear collider.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the charge transfer inefficiencies are low enough that a CCD detector would be a viable option for a future high-energy collider experiment.
a CCD operating at 250 K with a readout frequency of 7-50MHz should be capable of operating with an acceptable charge transfer inefficiency in a particle detector in an ILC environment.
the CCDs are a very promising candidate for the pixelated tracking detector in the ILC vertex detector, and that a detailed study of the radiation tolerance of the CCDs should be performed.

the LCFI detector concept, with the proposed pixelated vertex detector (PVD) and a high-speed serial readout CCD, has been proven to be a viable option for the ILC vertex detector.

the simulations of the temperature dependence of the CTE for a prototype serial read out CCD chip show that operation at about 250K is the optimum temperature for the chip.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temperature of the CCD should be kept as low as possible, but not so low as to cause the CCD to freeze.
the charge transfer inefficiencies in the CCDs can be reduced by operating the CCD at lower temperatures and that the effect of operating the CCD at higher frequencies than 50 MHz is small.
the CCDs can be used in a future particle detector at the ILC with a readout frequency of 7 MHz and at temperatures above 150 K.
